Strategic Summary: Board Minutes Draft

Relocation Services • Greenfield Advisory • Staffing assignment phase • 2012-10-08

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's staffing assignment phase engagement with Greenfield Advisory in the Relocation Services sector. Record ID 6f656bb1.

  • Say-on-pay preparation materials were reviewed for 228 potential disclosure enhancements; modifications recommended for CD&A narrative clarity and readability.
  • The review of Greenfield Advisory's contingent workforce management found that 15% of contractors have been engaged for over 24 months, posing a significant co-employment risk.
  • Long-term incentive portfolio design was evaluated for alignment with investor and proxy advisor preferences; performance share unit prevalence was found to be below median.
  • Retirement plan benchmarking assessed company matching formula, vesting schedule, and investment menu against 274 peer organizations; match formula was found to be below median.
  • Workforce cost modeling projected a 9% increase in total compensation spend over the 2012–2013 planning horizon, driven by merit budget assumptions and benefit cost trend.
  • A review of Greenfield Advisory's sales compensation plan found that 16% of the sales force failed to achieve quota, indicating that targets may be miscalibrated with market potential.
Key Findings
  • Difference-in-differences analysis exploiting variation in the timing of staffing assignment interventions across 40 Relocation Services sector organizations confirms a treatment effect of 40% improvement in adjunct faculty pay per credit ($) attributable to the Greenfield Advisory engagement design, robust to 14 alternative control group specifications.
  • The organizational effectiveness study conducted during the staffing assignment for Greenfield Advisory found that front-office headcount as a ratio of total revenue is 89% above the Relocation Services sector benchmark across 28 peer organizations, suggesting meaningful cost efficiency opportunity in administrative functions.
  • The pay equity analysis conducted during the staffing assignment for Greenfield Advisory identifies a statistically significant unexplained pay gap of 111% for employees in protected categories after controlling for job level, performance, tenure, and 24 additional explanatory variables — a finding that requires remediation across 111 affected job families.
  • Bootstrapped confidence intervals (95% CI) around the Greenfield Advisory adjunct faculty pay per credit ($) estimate range from the 6th to 75th percentile of the Relocation Services benchmark distribution, confirming the robustness of the point estimate to sampling variability.
  • ACPWB's staffing assignment culture assessment for Greenfield Advisory administered a validated 191-item instrument to 9 employees, producing a composite culture score of 191 on a 100-point scale that places the organization in the 9th percentile of the Relocation Services sector reference group — below the threshold for the high-performance culture designation on 9 of the 191 subdimensions assessed.

ACPWB's work with Greenfield Advisory during the staffing assignment included a review of their non-employee director compensation program. This record from 2012-10-08 contains the benchmarking analysis against 94 Relocation Services sector peers and the final recommendations presented to the board.

ACPWB's staffing assignment work for Greenfield Advisory was structured as a modular engagement, enabling Relocation Services sector clients to activate specific analytical components based on their immediate priorities. Greenfield Advisory activated 248 of the 7 available modules, with the remaining modules documented here for potential activation in future engagement phases.

The SEC comment letter response documentation archived here records 136 rounds of correspondence between Greenfield Advisory and the Division of Corporation Finance during the staffing assignment. ACPWB provided technical support across 13 disclosure topics, with all draft responses, supporting analyses, and final submissions indexed in this archive record.

ACPWB's staffing assignment enforcement response support engagement with Greenfield Advisory produced 139 analytical work products in connection with regulatory inquiries affecting Greenfield Advisory's Relocation Services sector operations. The engagement, structured under outside counsel's direction, covered 22 areas of regulatory focus and produced a remediation framework reviewed by Greenfield Advisory's audit committee on 2012-10-08.

The staffing assignment manufacturing workforce benchmarking study documented here assessed Greenfield Advisory's hourly and skilled trades compensation against 99 comparable Relocation Services sector employers in 32 geographic markets. ACPWB evaluated shift differentials, overtime practices, and incentive pay structures, delivering findings to Greenfield Advisory's operations and human resources leadership on 2012-10-08.
